scoreNotes.shapeVolume: The original square three-board stool and splayed supports are preserved; seat rim/corners and leg shading are softer than the source, but the large seat face still reads as a flat panel.
scoreNotes.color: Honey yellow/gold and warm brown remain coherent and the supports no longer disappear into near-black. The seat interior has almost no highlight-to-midtone range.
scoreNotes.lightingHighlights: Directionally coherent, softly shaded front rim and no ground shadow. Broad subdued face highlights and gradual face transitions required by the frozen criteria are not yet visible.
scoreNotes.materialDetail: Two seams remain legible in every facing, but are visually uniform thin orange lines across a nearly uniform yellow face rather than convincing softly inset board separations.
scoreNotes.artifactFreeReadability: Clean alpha, no isolated colored pixels, clipping, unwanted ground shadow or broken structural joins seen on the required light/gray/dark backgrounds or logical-size/repeated previews.

observations: All four actual 384x704 native images and all six packet previews were inspected; the logical-size preview confirms the stool identity, supports and two board seams remain readable at 192x352.

Relative to the original, the hard stepped seat perimeter is replaced by a smooth rounded transition, the orange front edge has a softer ramp, and the legs/stretcher retain useful warm brown midtones instead of the source dark mass. These are visible improvements.

The fixed target derives much of its soft wood volume from broad tonal variation within each board, softly modeled inset seam lips, and restrained wide highlights. The candidate face instead reads as one flat golden fill with two thin lines; most shading is confined to the lowest rim.

This flatness is visible on all backgrounds and at logical size. A descriptive check of the submitted S interior (x130:254, y315:445, excluding seam rows) found channel ranges R255:255, G204:206, B88:90. This measurement corroborates the direct pixel impression; it is not an invented numeric approval threshold.

N/S and E/W are coherent native rotations: the board seam direction changes with the geometry while the overall neutral lighting remains consistent. The source square proportions are retained without copying the target enlargement or stray luminous outline.

blockers.location: Large upper seat face in N/E/S/W, including the three board interiors and the transitions beside the two seam lines.
blockers.effect: The seat is dominated by one nearly uniform bright yellow patch. It lacks the broad restrained highlight/midtone modeling required by frozen color and lightingHighlights criteria, so the central visual mass still feels flat despite the softened outline. The two uniform seam hairlines reinforce that flat-panel impression.
blockers.desiredVisibleOutcome: Retain the registered square seat, socket height and neutral horizontal lighting, while making broad gentle honey-gold highlight-to-midtone variation visibly model the board faces and softly inset seams at logical sprite size. Keep the variation restrained, the wood matte/satin, and the board layout clear; do not add a unilateral shine, noisy grain, bright outline, target widening or ground shadow.

remainingDifferences: The source seat remains square and its supports retain the source silhouette rather than adopting the target broader puffed outline; this is required by the source contract.
No fine target grain or target alpha glow is required. The candidate clean alpha is preferable to the target isolated edge pixels.
Lower supports are somewhat simpler and lighter than the target, but remain warm, continuous and legible; they are not the current material blocker.
